 Two more banks change fixed deposit rates: 5 interesting takeaways from their latest interest tables
 By Upstox News Desk 5 min read | Updated on November 13, 2026, 17:31 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 The two banks differ sharply in the medium terms. While Federal Bank is offering a premium for 12-to-24 month deposits, Bank of Baroda's best rates are in its special 444-day and 555-day schemes.
 Federal Bank, Bank of Baroda have increased FD rates. | Image: Shutterstock
 Two more banks - Bank of Baroda and Federal Bank - have joined the list of four banks that have revised their fixed deposit interest rates in November.
T
he two banks are offering general citizens between 6.25% and 6.85% at the top of their standard fixed deposit ladders, with 0.50% to 1% more interest for senior citizens, depending on the tenure and the scheme.

 The two banks differ sharply in the medium terms. While Federal Bank is offering a premium for 12-to-24 month deposits, Bank of Baroda's best rates are in its special 444-day and 555-day schemes.

 5 interesting takeaways
 First, Federal Bank's 181-day bucket pays 6.00% while its 182-to-270-day bucket pays 5.50%, which is like a 50-basis-point difference decided by a single day. One that makes the shorter deposit, gets the better deal.
 Second, Federal Bank's sweet spot is 12 to 24 months as it offers 6.55% for above one year to under 15 months, 6.65% at exactly 15 months and 6.55% again up to 24 months. All of these rates well above Bank of Baroda's 6.25% for the same tenures.
 Third, Bank of Baroda's senior citizen rate rises with tenure. The bank’s website shows 0.50% extra interest for resident senior citizens up to three years, 0.60% for above three to five years, and a full 1.00% for over five to 10 years, allowing seniors to earn 7.00% interest against the general public's 6.00%. Super senior citizens get a further 0.10% on deposits above one year and up to five years.
 Fourth, Federal Bank pays a flat 0.50% more to senior citizens across every bucket. Its non-callable Deposit Plus variant for deposits of ₹1 crore and above adds 10 to 20 basis points more, offering 6.85% at 48 months for the public and 7.35% for senior citizens.
 Fifth, the special schemes carry the best headline rates at Bank of Baroda. The 555-day bob Golden Goal pays 6.75% to the public and 7.35% to super senior citizens, ahead of the 444-day bob Square Drive's 6.45% and 7.05%.
